# Can a cell that has stopped dividing start again?

<!-- STEP id="carrot-root" -->
## A carrot root grows

A carrot root grows longer because cells near its tip divide again and again. This group of dividing cells is a meristem. The new cells left behind the tip grow larger and change, and each kind takes up one job.

<!-- STEP id="cells-stop" -->
## Cells that stop dividing

Some of the new cells become phloem, which carries food. Others become storage cells, which fill the orange root with food. Once a cell has taken up a job like this, it stops dividing, and it is part of a permanent tissue.

**Inside the carrot, its phloem cells do not divide.**

Suppose a few of these phloem cells are taken out of the carrot and kept in a flask with food. Can a cell that has stopped dividing ever divide again?
